title: Neeru Dhanda Leads India's Sign-Off as Asian Games Close in Aichi-Nagoya
excerpt: Trap shooter Neeru Dhanda, with two golds and a silver, carried the tricolour at Nagoya's Mizuho Park Stadium as India finished fourth with 85 medals — its second-best Asian Games tally.
body:
• The 2026 Asian Games closed on Sunday at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Nagoya, ending 16 days of competition across Aichi-Nagoya featuring athletes from 45 countries and regions.
  • Trap shooter Neeru Dhanda, 27, carried India's tricolour as flag-Bearer: she won two gold medals and a silver, becoming the first Indian woman to win an individual Asian Games gold in trap shooting.
  • India finished fourth overall with 85 medals — 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze — its second-best Asian Games tally ever.
  • China topped the table with 341 medals (169 gold), followed by hosts Japan with 269 (83 gold) and South Korea with 150 (39 gold); the Olympic Council of Asia flag was handed over to Doha, host of the 2030 Games.

Trap shooter Neeru Dhanda carried the Indian tricolour at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Sunday, leading a 495-strong contingent off the stage of the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium after India's second-best medal haul in the event's history. The Indian Olympic Association named the 27-year-old as the country's flag-Bearer, and deputy chef de mission Anjali Bhagwat confirmed the selection — asking Dhanda, who had already returned to India, to travel back to Japan for the honour.

The ceremony, which began at 6pm local time (2:30pm IST) after a warm-up stage of Japanese performers, closed 16 days of competition across 36 disciplines. The Olympic Council of Asia flag was formally handed over to representatives of the Doha 2030 organising committee, with Qatar's Olympic and world champion high jumper Mutaz Bashim featuring in the handover segment, the Associated Press reported.

Dhanda's record campaign

Dhanda was an obvious choice to lead the parade. She won the women's individual trap event with a score of 26 after setting an Asian Games record in qualification — missing just two shots out of 30 for 28 — becoming the first Indian woman to win an individual Asian Games gold in trap shooting. She followed it with silver in the women's trap team event alongside Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer, then partnered Kynan Chenai to gold in the mixed trap team event with another Asian Games record, scoring 34 to surpass the previous mark of 30 held by Qatar. It was India's first gold in the mixed team trap event at the Games.

India's 85-medal finish

India concluded its campaign with 85 medals — 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze — finishing fourth in the overall standings, according to ANI and multiple wire tallies. China dominated with 341 medals including 169 gold, hosts Japan took 269 with 83 gold, and South Korea was third with 150 medals including 39 gold. The Olympic Council of Asia cited 54 world records across the Games as evidence of the competition's quality, declaring Aichi-Nagoya a success.

Archery was India's most productive discipline with five gold medals; boxing contributed three and wrestling two. Both the men's and women's cricket teams won gold, completing a rare double, and golfer Pranavi Urs won India's first women's individual Asian Games gold in the sport. The final tally fell short of India's record 107 medals at Hangzhou 2023 but comfortably marks the second-best return in the country's Asian Games history.

A troubled Games, completed

The Aichi-Nagoya edition was dogged by logistical criticism throughout — transport problems, long distances between venues, no centralised athletes' village and sparse crowds drew complaints from delegations and media. The Olympic Council of Asia acknowledged the chaos but pointed to the completed competition calendar and the record marks as the story that mattered. All competitions finished on schedule and the closing ceremony arrived on time.

What's next

The Games now move to Doha 2030, the 21st edition, where India's shooters, archers and boxers will be expected to defend a tally that places the country firmly among Asia's top four sporting nations. For Dhanda, the flag-bearing role caps a Games that established her as the face of India's shooting programme — one more cycle from Los Angeles 2028, where trap gold will be firmly in her sights.
